es: Revisar un borrador y corregir seis problemas de registro, cohesión y matiz, cambiando lo vago por datos exactos y las afirmaciones exageradas por otras ajustadas.

teaching.en: In an email to the director, a formal register opens with Dear Ms Lopez, not Hi all, and avoids slang.
teaching.es: En un correo a la directora, un registro formal empieza con Dear Ms Lopez, no con Hi all, y evita la jerga.
teaching.explanationEs: Register: el saludo y las palabras deben encajar con quien lee.
segments: In an email to the director, a formal register opens
with Dear Ms Lopez, not Hi all, and avoids slang.
teaching.audioText: In an email to the director, a formal register opens with Dear Ms Lopez, not Hi all, and avoids slang.

teaching.en: To hedge a claim, write 'many students seem to dislike it', because 'everyone hates it' would overstate the evidence.
teaching.es: Para matizar una afirmación, escribe «a muchos estudiantes parece no gustarles», porque «todos lo odian» exageraría la evidencia.
teaching.explanationEs: Overstate = exagerar. Sustituye todos/nadie por many/some y añade seem to o appear to.
segments: To hedge a claim, write 'many students seem to dislike
it', because 'everyone hates it' would overstate the evidence.
teaching.audioText: To hedge a claim, write 'many students seem to dislike it', because 'everyone hates it' would overstate the evidence.

teaching.en: A linker such as however or so gives a text cohesion, whereas a run-on sentence joins ideas with nothing but commas.
teaching.es: Un conector como however o so da cohesión a un texto, mientras que una oración encadenada une ideas solo con comas.
teaching.explanationEs: Cohesion: los conectores (so, however, although) enlazan ideas. Run-on sentence: «The price rose, students complained» necesita linker o punto.
segments: A linker such as however or so gives a text cohesion,
whereas a run-on sentence joins ideas with nothing but commas.
teaching.audioText: A linker such as however or so gives a text cohesion, whereas a run-on sentence joins ideas with nothing but commas.

teaching.en: Vague words like soon or several should become precise details, such as by Friday or three complaints.
teaching.es: Las palabras vagas como soon o several deben convertirse en datos precisos, como by Friday o three complaints.
teaching.explanationEs: Vague = impreciso. Un plazo con fecha y una cifra son más útiles que un adverbio.
segments: Vague words like soon or several should become precise
details, such as by Friday or three complaints.
teaching.audioText: Vague words like soon or several should become precise details, such as by Friday or three complaints.

teaching.en: When you revise a draft, tighten up the wording by cutting filler, but do not water down the point you are making.
teaching.es: Al revisar un borrador, ajusta la redacción eliminando el relleno, pero no diluyas la idea que defiendes.
teaching.explanationEs: Tighten up = hacer más conciso. Water down = rebajar la fuerza de una idea; matizar no es diluir.
segments: When you revise a draft, tighten up the wording by cutting
filler, but do not water down the point you are making.
teaching.audioText: When you revise a draft, tighten up the wording by cutting filler, but do not water down the point you are making.

teaching.en: Every change must earn its place: if a new word is merely a synonym and adds nothing, leave the draft as it was.
teaching.es: Cada cambio debe justificarse: si una palabra nueva es solo un sinónimo y no aporta nada, deja el borrador como estaba.
teaching.explanationEs: Un cambio vale solo si mejora el registro, la cohesión o el matiz.
segments: Every change must earn its place: if a new word is merely
a synonym and adds nothing, leave the draft as it was.
teaching.audioText: Every change must earn its place: if a new word is merely a synonym and adds nothing, leave the draft as it was.

prompt.es: ¿Qué corrección mejora el registro del saludo a la directora?

choices.text: Hello everybody, I am writing about the school canteen.
Dear Ms Lopez, I am writing about the school canteen.
Dear Ms Lopez, hiya, I am writing about the school canteen.

feedback.es: El saludo debe dirigirse a la persona que lee y mantenerse formal de principio a fin. Hello everybody sigue siendo informal, y la tercera mezcla registros.

hint.es: Piensa a quién va dirigido el mensaje: la directora.

origin.text: Draft: Hi all! I am writing about the school canteen, because the food is a problem and the director must read this today.

prompt.es: Completa: «A muchos estudiantes parece no gustarles el nuevo menú.»

feedback.es: Seem to + verbo matiza la afirmación: no dice que todos lo odian, sino que parece que a muchos no les gusta.

hint.es: Es el verbo que atenúa: «parece que», no «es seguro que».

origin.text: The survey covered only thirty students from one class, so the writer should not overstate the result. A more careful version is: Many students ___ to dislike the new menu.

prompt.es: ¿Qué reescritura sustituye lo vago por datos precisos?

choices.text: We will ask the director very soon, and many students have already complained.
We will ask the director in due course, and some students have already complained.
We will ask the director by Friday, and three students have already complained.

feedback.es: Un día y una cifra son datos precisos. «Very soon», «many», «in due course» y «some» suenan distinto, pero siguen sin decir cuándo ni cuántos.

hint.es: Un dato preciso es un día y una cifra, no un adverbio más formal.

origin.text: Draft: We will ask the director soon, and several students have already complained.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Aunque el precio ha subido, muchos estudiantes parecen satisfechos.»

answer.text: Although the price has risen many students seem satisfied
accepted: Although the price has risen many students seem satisfied
Many students seem satisfied although the price has risen

feedback.es: Although une las dos ideas en una sola frase y seem matiza la segunda; el orden inverso con la subordinada al final también es correcto.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué consigue la editora con el cambio.

choices.text: She makes the claim easier to support without changing its direction.
She turns the writer's opinion about the rule into its opposite.
She makes the tone more formal but no less exaggerated.

feedback.es: Cambia «disaster» y «nobody» por «some families» y «few parents»: la dirección es la misma, pero ahora se puede probar. No invierte la opinión ni conserva la exageración.

origin.audio: The first draft said that the new rule was a disaster and that nobody supported it. The editor replaced both phrases: the rule has caused problems for some families, and few parents have spoken in its favour. The meaning is similar, but the claim is now one that the writer can back up with evidence.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada edición con el problema que corrige.

pairs: The price rose. Students complained. → The price rose, so students complained.

pairs.es: Mejora la cohesión con un conector

pairs: Everyone hates it → Many seem to dislike it
We will ask soon → We will ask by Friday

pairs.es: Sustituye lo vago por un dato preciso

feedback.es: Cada edición corrige un problema distinto: registro, cohesión, exageración y vaguedad.

pairs.es: Mejora la cohesión con un conector

pairs: Everyone hates it → Many seem to dislike it

prompt.es: ¿Qué lista resume los problemas principales del borrador?

choices.text: A casual greeting, overstated claims, a vague deadline and too many long sentences.
A casual greeting, overstated claims, a vague deadline and very short sentences.
A stiff greeting, cautious claims and a precise but impolite deadline.

feedback.es: Abre con «Hi all», exagera («everyone hates it», «obviously»), deja un plazo vago («soon») y encadena frases cortas sin conectores. Las frases no son largas ni el saludo es rígido.

origin.text: Hi all. The school food is terrible and everyone hates it. The new menu is obviously better. Students like it. The price went up. The cooks say they are sorry. We must change the menu now. The director must read this today. We will ask her soon. Last week, two students were ill after lunch. The parents are angry. Nobody wants to wait in a long line. The teachers say that the new menu has fewer vegetables, and some parents say that it costs too much. Thank you.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la editora suaviza la segunda frase.

choices.text: Because the director dislikes strong opinions.
Because the claim was not formal enough.
Because the survey only supports a weaker claim.

feedback.es: Suaviza porque la encuesta solo respalda «many students seem to dislike»: el matiz ajusta la frase a la evidencia, no al gusto de la directora ni al registro.

origin.audio: I changed the greeting from Hi all to Dear Ms Lopez, because the reader is the director. Then I softened the second sentence. Everyone hates the food became many students seem to dislike the food, which the survey actually supports. Finally, I joined the two short sentences with so, and I replaced soon with by Friday.

prompt.es: Completa: «Para dejar el texto más conciso, hay que recortar dos frases.»

feedback.es: Tighten up es la colocación natural para hacer un texto más conciso eliminando lo que sobra.

origin.text: The second paragraph repeats the same point three times. To ___ up the text, the writer should cut two of the sentences and keep the clearest one.

prompt.es: Reescribe el borrador como un solo mensaje formal a la directora.

answer.text: Dear Ms Lopez, many students seem to dislike the canteen food, and the price has risen, so we would be grateful if you could review the menu by Friday.
accepted: Dear Ms Lopez, many students seem to dislike the canteen food, and the price has risen, so we would be grateful if you could review the menu by Friday.
Dear Ms Lopez, it appears that many students dislike the canteen food, and the price has gone up; therefore, we would ask you to change the menu by Friday.
Dear Ms Lopez, some students seem unhappy with the food in the canteen, and the price has risen, so please review the menu before Friday.

feedback.es: Un mensaje editado abre con saludo formal, matiza «everyone hates» con seem to o many, une las ideas con un conector y fija un plazo exacto.

origin.text: Hi all. The canteen food is terrible and everyone hates it. The price went up. We will ask the director soon. Nobody listens to us.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión aporta cohesión y deja claro el contraste?

choices.text: The price rose; however, students still seem to like the menu, and the cooks say they are sorry.
The price rose, students still like the menu, the cooks say they are sorry.
The price rose and students still like the menu so the cooks say they are sorry about it today, which is why they have changed it.

feedback.es: However marca el contraste y and suma la última idea. La versión con solo comas es una oración encadenada, y la que usa so establece una causa ilógica.

origin.text: Draft: The price rose. Students still like the menu. The cooks say they are sorry.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué principio aplica la editora.

choices.text: That negative results should never appear in formal writing.
That a precise figure is stronger than an exaggerated judgement.
That a complaint only counts if a majority makes it.

feedback.es: Las preguntas de la editora sustituyen un juicio exagerado por un dato (doce de doscientos). No se prohíbe lo negativo ni se exige una mayoría.

origin.audio: An editor reads a line in a draft: the results were obviously terrible. She asks the writer what exactly was terrible, how many people said so, and compared with what. The writer replies that only twelve parents complained out of two hundred. Together they change the sentence to: a small number of parents complained, and the school plans to reply by Friday.

prompt.es: Completa: «No quisimos diluir el punto principal.»

feedback.es: Water down significa rebajar la fuerza de una idea; tone down y play down son alternativas naturales.

origin.text: The director asked us to change the wording of our request, but we refused to ___ down the main point: the menu must change.
